payload.body: Task 3 approach. (1) fleet/launch.mjs: export vmSizeFor(widestWave, cap) — C = min(cap.cpu, 2+ceil(W/3)), M = min(capGB, 2+W), memory spelled <int>GB. settings.cpu/memory become the ceiling; an explicit --cpu/--memory still wins outright and every BASE refusal message is kept verbatim. (2) The --stamp compile moves out of fileRunOnHub into the launch body, once, right after the run number is read and before the new verb; the payload is passed down to fileRunOnHub. Because the stamp needs N, and sizing needs the payload, and the billing-plan check needs the size, the billing check moves to just after the compile (still before the credential refresh, the push and the verb, so a refusal still mutates nothing). (3) fleet/run-main.mjs: WIDTH becomes widthOf(args); boundedParallel(widthOf(launchArgs)). Known gap I will disclose: nothing can carry width= to the VM — COMMENT_KEYS lives in fleet/lobby.mjs (task 4's file) and parse_assignment in fleet/sandbox-boot.sh (which this run may only touch on overlap lines), and an unknown comment key fails every boot. So width rides the launch result and the fallback 12 is what production reads.

payload.author: exam:3@run-127
payload.body:
examiner (task 3): approach for fleet/tests/test_launch_size.mjs.

The rig is the deleted launch sims' (test_launch_compile.mjs / test_launch_kata.mjs, at b64ecc07^): a real bare origin from _lobby_helpers.mjs makeTargetRepo, every lobby verb and remote git answered by makeExec, python3 answered by a stub — '--check' answers 'PLAN OK', the '--stamp' call answers a canned payload with launch_waves. No socket is opened.

Legs as I read them:
(a) [M1] two launches under config {cpu:'6',memory:'8GB'}: a one-wave one-task stub must yield '--cpu 3 --memory 3GB' on the new verb, and a stub whose waves are 2/10/1 tasks (widest 10, thirteen tasks in all — so the exam reads the WIDEST WAVE, not the task count) must yield '--cpu 6 --memory 8GB'. Third launch under config {...FLEET_DEFAULTS} (what loadFleetConfig answers when there is no fleet.json) with the 2/10/1 stub: caps 8/16GB, so '--cpu 6 --memory 12GB'.
(b) [M2] '--cpu 2' with the 2/10/1 stub yields '--cpu 2', and — my reading, per-flag, which is BASE's opts.cpu ?? settings.cpu ?? default shape — memory stays the formula's '8GB'. The two billing refusals are pinned by exact message equality against BASE's strings.
(c) [M3] exactly one python3 call carrying '--stamp' per launch, ordered before the new verb, naming the plugin's own compile_plan.py, the plan path and '--base <base>', cwd the checkout. Run once with no hub (sizing alone must still drive the compile — M1 is unconditional) and once with a recording fake hub, where the filing's createIssue calls must cover exactly the stub's thirteen task ids: one payload, read by both.
(d) [M4] widthOf is read off a namespace import of ../run-main.mjs (not a named import, so a BASE that lacks the export fails as a missing export rather than a link error that hides every other leg): 4 for {width:4}, 12 for {} and 12 for {width:0}. The greps are done by reading fleet/run-main.mjs: no 'WIDTH = 12', and 'boundedParallel(widthOf(' present. For 'the launch arguments the fake sandbox receives carry width equal to the widest wave' the only thing a launch exam can see is the new call itself, so the assertion is over the new verb's argv AND its stdin (the setup script) together: it must carry width=1 for the one-task stub and width=10 for the 2/10/1 stub. Note for the implementer: lobby.mjs COMMENT_KEYS and setup-script.mjs are both outside this task's file scope, so the in-scope route is launch.mjs appending the pair to the assignment comment it builds.
(e) [M5] USAGE carries '[--cpu <n>]' and '[--memory <n>GB]'; RUNBOOK's '## One-time setup' section (to '## Per run') says ceiling and still names cpu, memory and fleet.json.
(f) [Produces] vmSizeFor(W, cap) is exported from launch.mjs and pure: the formula pinned at W = 1, 10, 100 under both cap pairs, answering {cpu, memory} as strings with memory spelled <int>GB.

Not pinned: fleet/CONTRACT.md's new-verb sentence — no Machine clause and no leg names it, so the exam leaves its wording to the implementer.

2. **leg (b) run** [M2] — the #908 path: a runnable exam that is red at BASE and stays red, so the pre-review pass buys `fix:A:0`; the fix reply is `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS` with an `exam:` concern, which buys review round 1; round 1 re-appends the red exam as blocking whatever the referee returns. Today that buys `fix:A:1` + round 2; with one round the task takes the `fix-loop-exhausted` exit that already exists. examiner (task 1, `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs`): the approach I am about to take.

The exam is one sim in the shape of `_engine_helpers.mjs`'s `rig` — real git, real clones, real fold, only `agent` stubbed — recording every prompt by label, plus a static read of the four source files for M4. Four engine runs, one per shape:

1. **legs (a), (c)** — a task with two green `Run:` lines, one green `Check:`, and a Proof `Test:` (`t1_test.sh`, testCmd `bash t1_test.sh`) so an examiner is dispatched. Asserts the recorded `impl:T1` prompt has no line beginning `TEST COMMAND:`, carries exactly one `\nPROOFS:\n` marker, and that the three lines `- Run: <a>`, `- Run: <b>`, `- Check: <c>` appear contiguously in that order — and that those three are the ONLY `- Run:`/`- Check:` lines anywhere in the prompt (the sim's task body deliberately carries none, so the count is honest). The `exam:T1` prompt is asserted to still carry `\nTEST COMMAND: bash t1_test.sh` and no `PROOFS:` block [M3].
2. **leg (b)** — same shape with the second `Run:` red, so the driver's pre-review pass buys `fix:T1:0`; the fix prompt is asserted by the same two predicates as the implementer's [M2].
3. **leg (a), second half** — a task with no `Run:` and a run with no `Check:`: the block is exactly `(none — the driver runs the exam at handoff)` and there are no bullet lines at all [M1].
4. **leg (e)** — the implementer writes a `BROKEN` marker (the rig's `check.sh` is `[ ! -f BROKEN ]`), so the folded candidate's suite is red once and a `reconcile:wave1:1` worker is dispatched; the stub removes the marker and reports FIXED. The recorded reconcile prompt is asserted to carry `\nTEST COMMAND: bash check.sh` — the run-wide command — and no `PROOFS:` block [M5].
5. **leg (d)** — a static read of `fleet/run-engine.mjs` for the four symbols and of both role files for `TEST COMMAND`, beside the Proof's two greps.

Expected at BASE: legs (a), (b) and (d) red (the engine still writes `TEST COMMAND:` and defines the four symbols); legs (c) and (e) GREEN at BASE on purpose — M3 and M5 are 'still, unchanged' clauses, and their passing is also what proves the sim itself is healthy rather than mis-wired. The file reports every leg and exits 1 if any failed, so the driver's red reads as the named clause, not as the first throw.

payload.author: exam:2@run-127
payload.body:
examiner reading — leg (a)'s lean half is not encodable as written, and why:

Leg (a) says "a \`lean\` task's [labels] hold none", and M1's gloss says "\`lean\` still means it is not [reviewed]". At BASE a lean task **is** reviewed — by exactly one reviewer, on the `reviewOpts()` branch with no pass number. Two survivor sims pin that in bytes:

- `test_run_engine_review_economy.mjs` (the driver-minted-red block) uses a default-`lean` task and asserts `calls` deep-equal `['impl:A', 'review:A:1', 'fix:A:1', 'review:A:2']`;
- every task in `test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs` is `review: 'lean'`, and its leg (b) asserts the order `['impl:T1', 'proof-run', 'review:T1:1']`.

`isPairReview` decides how MANY reviewers, not whether there is one. So making `lean` unreviewed would delete the reviewer from almost every leg of `test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs`, which M5 requires green — and M1's own first sentence ("Every review round dispatches exactly one worker ... **whatever the task's Review value is**") reads the other way. The gloss and the leg's lean half are a misreading of `isPairReview` as the review gate.

The exam therefore encodes, for the lean task, only what both readings agree on: no label ending `:1:1` or `:1:2`, no `review:B:*` label carrying a pass number, and at most one reviewer per round. The peer half of leg (a) is encoded in full and is red at BASE. The lean half is returned under `unsatisfiable`.

Second reading — leg (b): "a stub that keeps a proof red through the fix round ... reviewVerdict \`fix-loop-exhausted\`" can only be the #908 exam-concern path. A plain red `Run:` that survives `fix:<id>:0` never reaches a reviewer at all: it exits `reviewVerdict: 'proof-red'`, which `test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs` pins (its M1) and M5 keeps green. The one red that survives `fix:<id>:0` and still buys a review round is a red exam beside the fix round's `exam:` concern — and round 1 re-appends that red as blocking whatever the referee returns, which is exactly the Context's "the second red after \`fix:<id>:0\` takes the \`fix-loop-exhausted\` exit that exists today". The exam builds that scenario.

payload.body:
Done: all four Proof legs green (a: 0 overlap in the boot script; b: 0 across contract+runbook; c: bash -n clean and test_sandbox_boot_viz.mjs prints ALL TESTS PASSED; d: fleet/run-engine.mjs is the sole non-recursive match, its one line the fold comment). Full suite 130 passed.

Two decisions a later session would otherwise rediscover:

1. out-of-FILES: fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs:204 — the boot sim's own ASSIGNMENT fixture read 'overlap=fold tier=mostCapable'. Once the parser stops knowing the key it hits the unknown-key fail, so every sandbox-boot sim died at 'reading the assignment' until the fixture dropped the token. Proof leg (c) cannot pass without this edit, and leg (d)'s glob is non-recursive so fleet/tests/ is out of its reach either way.

2. The Global Constraint pins every added/removed line in sandbox-boot.sh to the word 'overlap'/'OVERLAP'. Four of the five sites are pure deletions and satisfy it exactly. The fifth, the assignment log at :697, is a field removal, so its diff is a -/+ pair: the removed line carries 'overlap=', the added one cannot, because M1 requires zero occurrences in the file. The task's own Context mandates this edit ('the log line keeps its other fields'), so the intended reading is the removed-line side; a literal every-line check would have no satisfiable implementation.

Left alone deliberately: the comment above run_engine() still says 'The three optional knobs as ARRAY elements' with only --tier and --implementer-effort left in knobs[]. Correcting the count would add a line carrying neither spelling of the word, which the Global Constraint forbids. It is stale prose, not behaviour.
